clips.send: Ganges River. A sacred river for Hindus, about 2,500 km long. The Buddha taught, and great Indian empires grew, in the Ganges plain.
clips.text: Ganges River. A sacred river for Hindus, about 2,500 km long. The Buddha taught, and great Indian empires grew, in the Ganges plain.

clips.send: Euphrates River. It flows about 2,800 km from the mountains of Türkiye through Syria and Iraq to the Persian Gulf. Ur, Uruk and Babylon stood beside it.
clips.text: Euphrates River. It flows about 2,800 km from the mountains of Türkiye through Syria and Iraq to the Persian Gulf. Ur, Uruk and Babylon stood beside it.

clips.send: Indus River. Pakistan’s lifeline. About 3,200 km from Tibet through northern India into Pakistan and the Arabian Sea. The ancient Indus Valley civilization (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro) grew up along it. Most of Pakistan’s farms depend on its irrigation canals; floods in 2022 covered a third of the country.

The ancient Indus Valley civilization (Harappa, Mohenjo-daro) grew up along it.. Most of Pakistan’s farms depend on its irrigation canals; floods in 2022 covered a third of the country.

clips.send: Egypt. The gift of the Nile. North-east corner of Africa; the Sinai Peninsula reaches into Asia, and the Suez Canal crosses it. About 95 percent of its 110 million people live in the narrow Nile valley and delta; the rest is desert. Farming with Nile water, natural gas, tourism (pyramids) and Suez Canal fees.
clips.text: Egypt. The gift of the Nile. North-east corner of Africa; the Sinai Peninsula reaches into Asia, and the Suez Canal crosses it.. About 95% of its 110 million people live in the narrow Nile valley and delta; the rest is desert.. Farming with Nile water, natural gas, tourism (pyramids) and Suez Canal fees.

clips.send: Afghanistan. A mountainous, landlocked crossroads. Landlocked between Iran, Pakistan, Central Asia and China; the Hindu Kush mountains cover much of it. Dry, with cold winters; farmers depend on snowmelt rivers. An old Silk Road crossroads; decades of war have left it one of the poorest countries.
clips.text: Afghanistan. A mountainous, landlocked crossroads. Landlocked between Iran, Pakistan, Central Asia and China; the Hindu Kush mountains cover much of it.. Dry, with cold winters; farmers depend on snowmelt rivers.. An old Silk Road crossroads; decades of war have left it one of the poorest countries.

clips.send: Lake Chad. A shallow lake on the edge of the Sahel that has shrunk by about 90 percent since the 1960s, because of drought and water taken for farming.
clips.text: Lake Chad. A shallow lake on the edge of the Sahel that has shrunk by about 90% since the 1960s, because of drought and water taken for farming.

clips.send: Sahara. The largest hot desert on Earth. About 9 million square kilometers across North Africa — roughly the size of the USA or China. Only about a quarter is sand dunes; most is rocky plateau and gravel plain. Daytime heat can pass 45 degrees Celsius , but nights can be near freezing; people live at oases and along the Nile. It splits Africa into North Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa; camel caravans once carried gold and salt across it.

Only about a quarter is sand dunes; most is rocky plateau and gravel plain.. Daytime heat can pass 45 °C, but nights can be near freezing; people live at oases and along the Nile.. It splits Africa into North Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa; camel caravans once carried gold and salt across it.

clips.send: Great Green Wall (Sahel). A project started in 2007 by African countries to plant a belt of trees and grassland about 8,000 km long across the Sahel, from Senegal to Djibouti, to hold back the desert.
clips.text: Great Green Wall (Sahel). A project started in 2007 by African countries to plant a belt of trees and grassland about 8,000 km long across the Sahel, from Senegal to Djibouti, to hold back the desert.

clips.send: Turkey (Türkiye). A bridge between Europe and Asia. Mostly in Asia (Anatolia) with a small part in Europe; Istanbul sits on both sides of the Bosporus strait. The Tigris and Euphrates begin in its mountains; its dams give it control of water downstream. Farming, textiles, cars and tourism; earthquakes are a major danger.

The Tigris and Euphrates begin in its mountains; its dams give it control of water downstream.. Farming, textiles, cars and tourism; earthquakes are a major danger.

clips.send: Congo River. Africa’s river with the most water — and the deepest river in the world (over 220 m). It crosses the equator twice as it arcs through the rainforest.
clips.text: Congo River. Africa’s river with the most water — and the deepest river in the world (over 220 m). It crosses the equator twice as it arcs through the rainforest.

clips.send: Niger River. West Africa’s great river. It flows in a big curve through Mali — past Timbuktu at the edge of the Sahara — and ends in the oil-rich Niger Delta in Nigeria.
clips.text: Niger River. West Africa’s great river. It flows in a big curve through Mali — past Timbuktu at the edge of the Sahara — and ends in the oil-rich Niger Delta in Nigeria.

clips.send: Sahara. The largest hot desert in the world, almost as big as the whole United States. Only a small part is sand dunes; most is rock and gravel.
clips.text: Sahara. The largest hot desert in the world, almost as big as the whole United States. Only a small part is sand dunes; most is rock and gravel.

clips.send: Kuwait. A small, oil-rich country at the top of the Persian Gulf. Iraq invaded it in 1990; when a US-led coalition drove Iraq’s army out in 1991, the retreating troops set more than 600 oil wells on fire.
clips.text: Kuwait. A small, oil-rich country at the top of the Persian Gulf. Iraq invaded it in 1990; when a US-led coalition drove Iraq’s army out in 1991, the retreating troops set more than 600 oil wells on fire.

clips.send: Sahel. A dry belt of grassland and thorny bushes along the southern edge of the Sahara. Drought and overuse can turn it into desert, so countries are planting a “Great Green Wall” of trees.
clips.text: Sahel. A dry belt of grassland and thorny bushes along the southern edge of the Sahara. Drought and overuse can turn it into desert, so countries are planting a “Great Green Wall” of trees.

clips.send: Iraq. A country along the Tigris and Euphrates rivers — the land of ancient Mesopotamia. In August 1990 Iraq’s army invaded Kuwait, and in 1991 a US-led coalition drove it out in the Persian Gulf War.
clips.text: Iraq. A country along the Tigris and Euphrates rivers — the land of ancient Mesopotamia. In August 1990 Iraq’s army invaded Kuwait, and in 1991 a US-led coalition drove it out in the Persian Gulf War.

clips.send: New Delhi. Capital of India. Greater Delhi has over 30 million people and is one of the world’s largest city areas.
clips.text: New Delhi. Capital of India. Greater Delhi has over 30 million people and is one of the world’s largest city areas.

clips.send: Persian Gulf. Gan Ying, sent by Ban Chao to find Rome, reached the Persian Gulf, the farthest west a Han envoy is known to have gone.
clips.text: Persian Gulf. Gan Ying, sent by Ban Chao to find Rome, reached the Persian Gulf, the farthest west a Han envoy is known to have gone.

clips.send: Yangtze River. From the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau to the East China Sea at Shanghai. It is a “golden waterway” full of ships.
clips.text: Yangtze River. From the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau to the East China Sea at Shanghai. It is a “golden waterway” full of ships.

clips.send: China. East Asia’s giant. Third- or fourth-largest country by area; it stretches from the Himalayas and deserts in the west to the Pacific coast. About 1.4 billion people, mostly in the wetter east along the Yangtze, Huang He and the coast. Coal, rare earths and hydropower; the world’s largest manufacturer and exporter. Faces air pollution, river pollution and floods; leads the world in solar and wind power.

clips.send: Tigris River. Faster and wilder than the Euphrates. Nineveh, the Assyrian capital, and later Baghdad were built on its banks.
clips.text: Tigris River. Faster and wilder than the Euphrates. Nineveh, the Assyrian capital, and later Baghdad were built on its banks.

clips.send: 乍得湖。萨赫勒边缘一个很浅的湖泊。由于干旱和大量引水灌溉，自20世纪60年代以来面积缩小了约百分之90。
clips.text: 乍得湖。萨赫勒边缘一个很浅的湖泊。由于干旱和大量引水灌溉，自20世纪60年代以来面积缩小了约90%。

clips.send: 土耳其。连接欧洲和亚洲的桥梁。大部分在亚洲（安纳托利亚），小部分在欧洲；伊斯坦布尔横跨博斯普鲁斯海峡两岸。底格里斯河和幼发拉底河发源于它的山区；它修建的水坝控制着下游的水量。农业、纺织、汽车和旅游业发达；地震是重大威胁。

clips.send: 北京。北京是我国的首都，全国的政治中心、文化中心。城市中心的故宫是明清两代的皇宫。

clips.send: 尼日尔河。西非的大河，在马里境内绕了一个大弯，流经撒哈拉沙漠边缘的廷巴克图，最后在尼日利亚盛产石油的尼日尔河三角洲入海。

clips.send: 尼罗河。全长约6650千米，是世界上最长的河流之一。它每年夏天泛滥，给田地留下肥沃的黑泥——“埃及是尼罗河的赠礼”。

clips.send: 波斯湾。班超派甘英出使大秦，他到达波斯湾，是汉朝使者所到最远的地方。
clips.text: 波斯湾。班超派甘英出使大秦，他到达波斯湾，是汉朝使者所到最远的地方。

clips.send: 几内亚湾。非洲西海岸的大海湾。赤道和本初子午线就在这片海面上相交（0 度 ，0 度 ）。

clips.send: 科威特。波斯湾顶端一个面积不大、石油丰富的国家。1990年伊拉克入侵科威特；1991年以美国为首的多国部队把伊拉克军队赶走时，撤退的伊军点燃了600多口油井。

clips.send: 长江。长江从青藏高原流到上海注入东海，是一条繁忙的“黄金水道”。
clips.text: 长江。长江从青藏高原流到上海注入东海，是一条繁忙的“黄金水道”。

clips.send: 绿色长城（萨赫勒）。非洲国家2007年发起的工程，计划在萨赫勒地区从塞内加尔到吉布提种出一条长约8000千米的林草带，阻挡沙漠扩张。

clips.send: 恒河。印度教徒心中的圣河，全长约2500千米。佛陀在恒河平原传教，印度的大帝国也在这里兴起。

clips.send: 地中海。被欧洲、非洲、亚洲环抱的近乎封闭的海，名字的意思是“陆地中间的海”。古埃及、古希腊和古罗马都在它的沿岸发展起来。

clips.send: 吉达。沙特阿拉伯在红海边的主要港口，每年数以百万计的朝觐者经这里前往麦加。
clips.text: 吉达。沙特阿拉伯在红海边的主要港口，每年数以百万计的朝觐者经这里前往麦加。

clips.send: 拉各斯。尼日利亚最大的城市和港口，濒临几内亚湾，是非洲发展最快的城市之一，人口超过1500万。
clips.text: 拉各斯。尼日利亚最大的城市和港口，濒临几内亚湾，是非洲发展最快的城市之一，人口超过1500万。

clips.send: 中国。东亚大国。面积居世界前列，从西部的喜马拉雅山和沙漠一直延伸到东部的太平洋沿岸。约 14 亿人口，大多住在东部湿润地区的长江、黄河流域和沿海。煤、稀土和水电资源丰富；是世界最大的制造业国家和出口国。面临空气污染、河流污染和洪水；太阳能和风能发电居世界首位。

clips.send: 底格里斯河。它比幼发拉底河水流更急。亚述的都城尼尼微，后来的巴格达，都建在它的岸边。
clips.text: 底格里斯河。它比幼发拉底河水流更急。亚述的都城尼尼微，后来的巴格达，都建在它的岸边。

clips.send: 幼发拉底河。它从土耳其的山区流出，经叙利亚、伊拉克注入波斯湾，全长约2800千米。乌尔、乌鲁克和巴比伦都建在它的岸边。
clips.text: 幼发拉底河。它从土耳其的山区流出，经叙利亚、伊拉克注入波斯湾，全长约2800千米。乌尔、乌鲁克和巴比伦都建在它的岸边。

clips.send: 阿特拉斯山脉。西北非的山墙。绵延约 2500 千米，横跨摩洛哥、阿尔及利亚和突尼斯；最高峰图卜卡勒峰海拔 4167 米。它们把多雨的地中海沿岸和撒哈拉沙漠隔开。湿润空气在北坡降雨，所以农田和城市分布在山脉与大海之间。

clips.send: 萨赫勒。撒哈拉沙漠南缘一条干旱的草原和灌木地带。干旱和过度利用会让土地变成沙漠，各国正在这里种植“绿色长城”。

clips.send: 阿拉伯半岛。世界上最大的半岛，大部分是沙漠。约610年，穆罕默德在这里的麦加开始传播伊斯兰教。
clips.text: 阿拉伯半岛。世界上最大的半岛，大部分是沙漠。约610年，穆罕默德在这里的麦加开始传播伊斯兰教。

clips.send: 日本海。日本与亚洲大陆之间的海。周围是日本、朝鲜半岛和俄罗斯。暖流和寒流在这里交汇，盛产鱼类和鱿鱼。冬季寒风经过这片海吸收水汽，在日本西海岸降下大雪。

clips.send: 恒河—布拉马普特拉河三角洲。世界上最大的三角洲，大部分在孟加拉国境内。三角洲上的孙德尔本斯红树林里生活着孟加拉虎。
clips.text: 恒河—布拉马普特拉河三角洲。世界上最大的三角洲，大部分在孟加拉国境内。三角洲上的孙德尔本斯红树林里生活着孟加拉虎。

clips.send: 利雅得。沙特阿拉伯首都，阿拉伯沙漠中部的绿洲城市，夏天白天气温常超过45 摄氏度 。
clips.text: 利雅得。沙特阿拉伯首都，阿拉伯沙漠中部的绿洲城市，夏天白天气温常超过45°C。

clips.send: 刚果河。非洲水量最大的河流，也是世界上最深的河流（超过220米）。它在雨林中划出一道弧线，两次穿过赤道。
clips.text: 刚果河。非洲水量最大的河流，也是世界上最深的河流（超过220米）。它在雨林中划出一道弧线，两次穿过赤道。

clips.send: 黄河。黄河流经黄土高原，带着大量泥沙流入渤海。中华文明最早在黄河中下游发展起来。
clips.text: 黄河。黄河流经黄土高原，带着大量泥沙流入渤海。中华文明最早在黄河中下游发展起来。

clips.send: 伊拉克。底格里斯河和幼发拉底河流经的国家，就是古代美索不达米亚的所在地。1990年8月，伊拉克军队入侵科威特；1991年，以美国为首的多国部队在海湾战争中把它赶了出去。

clips.send: 撒哈拉沙漠。世界上最大的热带沙漠，面积几乎和整个美国一样大。只有一小部分是沙丘，大部分是岩石和砾石。

clips.send: 新德里。印度首都。德里都市区人口超过3000万，是世界上最大的城市地区之一。
